title: pgbouncer pool exhaustion on ledger-db post v2.4 deploy
alert_text:
FATAL: sorry, too many clients already
[ERROR] pgbouncer pool exhaustion on db-primary-01.kirana.internal:6432. Active server connections: 200/200, queued clients: 84. Host: payments-worker-7d9b-x92zk.
symptoms: UPI settlement payouts failing with database connection timeouts; API latency spiked to 12.4s.
root_cause: payments-worker concurrency raised from 16 to 64 in v2.4 release without scaling pgbouncer default_pool_size (was 25). Each worker worker thread exhausted pool slots.
resolution_steps: Lowered PAYMENTS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY env var back to 16 in deployment manifest
Increased pgbouncer default_pool_size from 25 to 50 in pgbouncer.ini
Reloaded pgbouncer config: systemctl reload pgbouncer
what_did_not_work: Restarting payments-worker pods temporarily cleared connections but pool filled up again within ~10 minutes.

title: pgbouncer pool exhaustion on ledger-db during high sale traffic
alert_text:
FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
[CRITICAL] db-primary-02.kirana.internal reached max_connections limit. Client count: 350. Source: payments-worker pods.
symptoms: Merchant payout batches failing across North India region; 500 errors on /api/v1/ledger/balance.
root_cause: Unannounced deployment of payments-worker autoscaling rule (hpa maxReplicas 50) flooded pgbouncer pool limits during flash sale.
resolution_steps: Capped payments-worker hpa maxReplicas to 20
Set PAYMENTS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY to 12 per pod
Adjusted pgbouncer max_client_conn to 1000 and default_pool_size to 60
what_did_not_work: Pod restarts provided temporary relief for 8-10 minutes before connection pool choked again.

title: pgbouncer connection choke on ledger-db after async retry rollout
alert_text:
FATAL: sorry, too many clients already
[ERROR] pgbouncer pool max pool_size reached for database 'kirana_ledger'. active_clients=200 waiting_clients=142. Host: ledger-db-replica-01.
symptoms: Double-entry ledger validation failing, payments worker crashing with DB timeout exceptions.
root_cause: Async retry queue rollout spawned additional DB connection per retry worker, breaching pgbouncer client limits.
resolution_steps: Decreased PAYMENTS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY from 32 to 16
Increased pgbouncer default_pool_size from 50 to 80 in pgbouncer.ini
Applied pool connection recycling lifetime max_age = 1800
what_did_not_work: Bouncing pgbouncer and payments-worker pods only relieved pressure for ~10 minutes.

title: Redis maxmemory eviction storm on checkout-api
alert_text:
OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
[WARNING] redis-checkout-cluster node-3 memory usage 98.4%. Evicted 452,000 keys in 120s. Volatile-lru active.
symptoms: User cart sessions logged out abruptly; checkout dropoff rate jumped 40%.
root_cause: TTL config change set session TTL to 7 days instead of 2 hours, preventing normal key expiration and causing massive LRU eviction of active shopping carts.
resolution_steps: Reverted session TTL back to 7200 seconds in checkout config
Flushed stale persistent cart keys using redis-cli SCAN script with pattern 'session:legacy:*'
Increased Redis maxmemory limit to 16GB
what_did_not_work: Flushing all Redis keys destroyed valid active customer checkouts.

title: Redis maxmemory eviction storm on checkout-api cart session cache
alert_text:
OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
[ERROR] redis-cart-primary: memory limit reached (12GB/12GB). Eviction rate 3200 keys/sec.
symptoms: Checkout payload validation errors; empty cart reported by 15,000 active shoppers.
root_cause: Cart recommendation metadata added to session payload without TTL override, bloating key sizes by 8x and triggering maxmemory eviction.
resolution_steps: Disabled recommendation payload caching in checkout-api flag
Executed targeted EXPIRE script for high-size keys
Set explicit TTL of 3600 seconds on cart object payloads
what_did_not_work: Restarting Redis primary caused failover to replica which immediately hit memory ceiling.

title: Kafka consumer lag spike on search-indexer after partition rebalance
alert_text: [ALERT] KafkaConsumerLagHigh: consumer_group=search-indexer-prod, topic=catalog-updates, lag=458,920 messages. Rebalance in progress for 1800s.
symptoms: New products added by sellers not showing in store search results for over 1 hour.
root_cause: Dynamic consumer group membership caused stop-the-world rebalance cascades whenever pod autoscaler added or terminated a search-indexer instance.
resolution_steps: Configured static consumer group membership by pinning group.instance.id in indexer pod spec (e.g. group.instance.id=search-indexer-pod-1)
Increased session.timeout.ms from 10000 to 45000 in consumer config
what_did_not_work: Adding more search-indexer pods caused more rebalance loops and worsened consumer lag.

title: Kafka consumer group rebalance thrashing on search-indexer
alert_text: [ALERT] KafkaConsumerLagHigh: consumer_group=search-indexer-prod, topic=inventory-events, lag=612,000 messages. Member revoked due to poll timeout.
symptoms: Inventory update stream lagging; out-of-stock items listed as available on Kirana Cloud mobile app.
root_cause: Heavy bulk catalog import batch exceeded max.poll.interval.ms (300000ms), causing broker to kick consumer and trigger rebalance loop.
resolution_steps: Ensured static membership group.instance.id was correctly set on all search-indexer stateful pods
Increased max.poll.interval.ms to 900000ms and reduced max.poll.records to 250
what_did_not_work: Manually resetting offset to latest lost 50k inventory updates.

title: TLS certificate expiry on auth-gateway
alert_text:
SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED certificate has expired
[EMERGENCY] https://auth.kiranacloud.in SSL handshake failure. HTTP 525 Origin SSL Handshake Failed.
symptoms: All user logins, token validations, and merchant authentication failing globally.
root_cause: Cert-manager auto-renewal webhook failed silently due to an ingress controller API version mismatch during Kubernetes 1.28 cluster upgrade.
resolution_steps: Manually provisioned and uploaded wildcard TLS cert via Let's Encrypt ACME DNS-01 challenge
Updated secret auth-gateway-tls in namespace prod-auth
Patched cert-manager deployment ClusterIssuer API endpoint
what_did_not_work: Bouncing ingress-nginx pods did not fix the expired certificate secret.

title: Duplicate UPI payment callbacks caused by bad feature flag
alert_text:
DuplicateKeyException: UNIQUE constraint failed: ledger_entries.idempotency_key
[CRITICAL] payments-worker processing duplicate webhook callback for txn_upi_9941029.
symptoms: Merchants receiving double payout credits for single customer UPI payments; high ledger discrepancy alerts.
root_cause: Feature flag 'new_upi_retry_flow' was enabled globally without checking bank gateway webhook idempotency headers, causing retry worker to process callback twice.
resolution_steps: Immediately toggled OFF feature flag 'new_upi_retry_flow' in LaunchDarkly / internal flag engine
Ran ledger correction script fix_duplicate_upi_credits.py for affected transactions
Added strict redis idempotency check prior to database transaction start
what_did_not_work: Disabling payment gateway webhook endpoint blocked legitimate incoming payments.

title: Core DNS lookup failure in Kubernetes cluster
alert_text:
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND redis-auth.prod.svc.cluster.local
[ERROR] auth-gateway unable to resolve internal microservice hostnames.
symptoms: Inter-service RPC calls failing with 503 Service Unavailable across all web pods.
root_cause: CoreDNS pods memory throttled after spike in single-label DNS queries from a misconfigured monitoring agent.
resolution_steps: Increased CoreDNS deployment memory limit from 170Mi to 512Mi
Enabled CoreDNS autopath plugin to optimize cluster search domain lookups
what_did_not_work: Restarting node local DNS caches did not resolve upstream CoreDNS OOM kills.

title: Disk full on notifications-svc log volume
alert_text:
No space left on device: '/var/log/notifications/app.log'
[WARN] node-worker-08 disk usage 100% on /dev/sda1.
symptoms: WhatsApp and SMS transaction OTP notifications queued and failing to dispatch.
root_cause: Debug level logging left enabled after WhatsApp API integration testing, producing 50GB of raw logs in 12 hours and filling host disk.
resolution_steps: Truncated app.log files and cleared rotated logs
Set LOG_LEVEL=INFO in helm values for notifications-svc
Configured logrotate to retain max 5GB with daily rotation
what_did_not_work: Deleting active log file without truncating left file descriptor open, retaining disk space usage.

title: Third-party SMS Gateway (Gupshup) HTTP 504 timeouts
alert_text:
HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout from vendor endpoint api.sms-provider.com/v1/send
[ERROR] OTP dispatch failure rate 68%.
symptoms: Customers unable to receive 2FA login OTPs for merchant dashboard.
root_cause: Upstream telecom aggregator infrastructure degradation in Mumbai region causing SMS dispatch timeouts.
resolution_steps: Switched active SMS provider route in notifications-svc config from Primary (Gupshup) to Fallback (Twilio/Kaleyra)
Notified SMS vendor support team
what_did_not_work: Retrying failed requests on primary provider escalated queue backpressure.

title: Elasticsearch JVM Heap Garbage Collection pause on search-indexer
alert_text: [WARN] [o.e.m.j.JvmGcMonitorService] [es-node-02] gc [young] took [14.2s] which is longer than the threshold [500ms]
symptoms: Search queries timing out on product catalog; 408 Request Timeout returned to mobile clients.
root_cause: Unoptimized wildcard regex search query executed by bulk indexing script caused JVM heap allocation spike.
resolution_steps: Killed long-running regex queries in Elasticsearch task manager
Restricted max_clause_count in search cluster settings
Updated search query builder to force prefix queries instead of wildcards
what_did_not_work: Increasing ES heap size beyond 32GB caused longer Stop-The-World compressed OOPs GC pauses.

title: Rate limit exceeded on Razorpay payment gateway API
alert_text:
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit of 100 req/sec exceeded on /v1/orders
[ERROR] Razorpay SDK API Client error.
symptoms: Checkout page showing 'Payment Gateway Unavailable' during peak Sunday evening sale.
root_cause: Retry logic in payments-worker lacked exponential backoff with jitter, leading to thundering herd during minor API glitch.
resolution_steps: Updated payments-worker retry policy to Exponential Backoff with Decorrelated Jitter
Contacted Razorpay account manager to bump rate limit tier to 300 req/sec
what_did_not_work: Immediate linear retries flooded API gateway and kept rate limit window open.

title: JWT secret key mismatch following deployment
alert_text:
JsonWebTokenError: invalid signature
[ERROR] auth-gateway rejected 100% of user authentication tokens after release v3.1.0.
symptoms: All active logged-in users instantly logged out and unable to re-authenticate.
root_cause: Secrets manager sync script omitted trailing newline when updating JWT_SECRET_KEY in production Kubernetes secret.
resolution_steps: Re-synced JWT_SECRET_KEY secret from Vault without formatting truncation
Restarted auth-gateway pod deployment to pick up corrected environment variable
what_did_not_work: Rolling back auth-gateway deployment binary did not update the underlying Kubernetes secret.

title: Deadlock in PostgreSQL transaction isolation level on ledger-db
alert_text:
ERROR: deadlock detected
DETAIL: Process 41209 waits for ShareLock on transaction 88102; blocked by process 41215.
[ERROR] ledger-db lock contention.
symptoms: Merchant balance updates failing; database transaction rollback rate spiked to 15%.
root_cause: Concurrent ledger updates locked account_balances and ledger_entries tables in reverse order across two payment reconciliation jobs.
resolution_steps: Enforced uniform locking order (account_balances first, then ledger_entries) in ORM model methods
Added explicit statement_timeout = 5000ms for reconciliation worker connections
what_did_not_work: Increasing lock timeout caused transactions to pile up and exhaust connection handles.

title: Node.js Event Loop starvation in checkout-api due to sync JSON parsing
alert_text: [ALERT] NodeJSEventLoopDelayHigh: event_loop_delay_ms=4820ms on checkout-api-pod-4. HTTP response time p99 > 8000ms.
symptoms: High CPU utilization on checkout-api nodes despite low HTTP request throughput; healthchecks timing out.
root_cause: Synchronous JSON schema validation on giant 15MB inventory sync payload blocked Node.js single-threaded event loop.
resolution_steps: Offloaded payload parsing and validation to a dedicated worker_thread
Added maximum payload size limit (2MB) on incoming HTTP request body
what_did_not_work: Adding more CPU cores to pod spec did not relieve single-thread blocking execution.

title: Stale webhooks queue clogging RabbitMQ memory in notifications-svc
alert_text: [CRITICAL] RabbitMQ high memory watermark reached (85%). Alarm triggered, publishers throttled.
symptoms: Webhook notification dispatches stalled; partner merchant integrations missing order status events.
root_cause: Dead Letter Exchange (DLX) was missing TTL expiration on unroutable webhook messages, filling queue buffer.
resolution_steps: Purged unroutable messages in DLQ with x-message-ttl set to 86400000ms (24h)
Set x-max-length policy on webhook retry queue in RabbitMQ manager
what_did_not_work: Restarting RabbitMQ broker node caused memory dump to disk and delayed startup by 20 minutes.
